note: Niue, read in the Consolidated Niue Legislation the Government publishes on gov.nu (laws in force as at 31 December 2019, updated to 2022, with the 2021-2024 supplements listed), 2026-10-31. Majority: no Act in the Legislation Tables sets an age of majority; the Minors' Contracts Act 1969 (NZ, in force in Niue from 1 January 1970, as consolidated in volume 2) makes contracts of minors of 18 or over binding as if of full age, save those a court finds unconscionable, and governs those under 18 (ss. 5-6), while the Guardianship Part of the Niue law in the same volume calls a child a person under 20; full age itself isn't defined in what was read, so majority is null (contractual capacity from 18 isn't held as majority; a reading to check). Work: the Legislation Tables list no Act on employment standards or children's employment (only the Niue Public Service Act), so no minimum age was found and work is null. Service: Niue has no armed forces and no Act in the tables deals with military service, so service is none (a reading from absence).

sources.title: Consolidated Niue Legislation 2019, volume 2 (gov.nu)
sources.said: MINORS’ CONTRACTS ACT 1969 ... Contracts of minors of or over the age of 18 ... “child” means a person under the age of 20 years;
